column2: The time has come to celebrate Thanksgiving, the ancient holiday where Americanists of all stripes come together and feast in the name of brotherhood and, well, thanksgiving.
Your vassals are invited to a Thanksgiving feast.

Over a millennium ago, the first freedom-seeking pilgrims arrived on the shores of this great nation. They were nearly wiped out in their first winter, but the first Americanist Founder, Squanto, taught them how to properly cultivate the land. He planted the seeds of both their crops and Americanism itself.
You send invitations to your freedom-loving vassals.
You have been invited to join [From.GetTitledFirstName] at his Thanksgiving dinner this year. It is an occasion where theological debates are strictly prohibited in the name of peace and brotherhood.
You decline to attend the Thanksgiving dinner.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has refused your invitation to the Thanksgiving dinner, claiming [From.GetSheHe] has other plans.

The Thanksgiving dinner has begun in earnest. As is tradition, guests casually dine on appetizers before a fat turkey is slaughtered, cooked, and stuffed to act as the main course. After a brief prayer of thanks to the Founding Fathers for America's great bounty, you and your guests eagerly dig in.
The dinner lasts well into the night, but it eventually comes to an end. As your stuffed and drowsy guests stumble home, you can hear them murmur that this dinner was especially filling.
The dinner lasts well into the night, but it eventually comes to an end. As you drowsily stumble your way back to your carriage, you can hear the other guests murmur about how good this dinner was.
